name: Capes, Panels and Manga: A History of Comics
description: How a 1938 comic book with a man lifting a car launched the superhero, and how newspaper strips, manga and graphic novels grew into a world art form.

checkpoints.name: The funny pages
checkpoints.note: Newspapers filled their Sunday pages with colour strips such as The Yellow Kid, Little Nemo and Krazy Kat, and in Belgium Tintin began his adventures in 1929, before the comic book itself took shape.

checkpoints.name: The golden age
checkpoints.note: A new company, a strong man from another planet and a bat-suited detective launched comic books as a mass medium, and soon heroes were fighting the Second World War.

checkpoints.name: The backlash
checkpoints.note: A psychiatrist's book and a Senate hearing blamed comics for crime among the young, and publishers adopted a strict code that kept the stories tame. Meanwhile Peanuts won newspaper readers and Asterix began in France in 1959.

checkpoints.name: The Marvel revolution
checkpoints.note: Stan Lee and Jack Kirby gave heroes everyday troubles and hit a nerve. Meanwhile Japan's manga grew, with Doraemon from 1969, and a Holocaust memoir, Maus, showed what comics could say.

checkpoints.name: Grown-up comics
checkpoints.note: Darker, more thoughtful comics such as Watchmen and The Dark Knight Returns won adult readers, while manga such as Dragon Ball, Sailor Moon, One Piece and Naruto reached readers around the world, and Persepolis told a childhood in Iran.
